_provenance.title: National curriculum in England: design and technology programmes of study

_provenance.scope: Statutory programme-of-study statements only (the 'Pupils should be taught' lists), verbatim. Non-statutory notes and guidance, aims, purpose of study and appendices are not included.

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: design purposeful, functional, appealing products for themselves and other users based on design criteria

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: generate, develop, model and communicate their ideas through talking, drawing, templates, mock-ups and, where appropriate, information and communication technology

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: select from and use a range of tools and equipment to perform practical tasks [for example, cutting, shaping, joining and finishing]

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: select from and use a wide range of materials and components, including construction materials, textiles and ingredients, according to their characteristics

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: explore and evaluate a range of existing products

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: evaluate their ideas and products against design criteria

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: build structures, exploring how they can be made stronger, stiffer and more stable

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: explore and use mechanisms [for example, levers, sliders, wheels and axles] in their products

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: use research and develop design criteria to inform the design of innovative, functional, appealing products that are fit for purpose, aimed at particular individuals or groups

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: generate, develop, model and communicate their ideas through discussion, annotated sketches, cross-sectional and exploded diagrams, prototypes, pattern pieces and computer-aided design

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: select from and use a wider range of tools and equipment to perform practical tasks [for example, cutting, shaping, joining and finishing], accurately

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: select from and use a wider range of materials and components, including construction materials, textiles and ingredients, according to their functional properties and aesthetic qualities

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: investigate and analyse a range of existing products

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: evaluate their ideas and products against their own design criteria and consider the views of others to improve their work

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand how key events and individuals in design and technology have helped shape the world

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: apply their understanding of how to strengthen, stiffen and reinforce more complex structures

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand and use mechanical systems in their products [for example, gears, pulleys, cams, levers and linkages]

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand and use electrical systems in their products [for example, series circuits incorporating switches, bulbs, buzzers and motors]

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: apply their understanding of computing to program, monitor and control their products

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: use research and exploration, such as the study of different cultures, to identify and understand user needs

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: identify and solve their own design problems and understand how to reformulate problems given to them

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: develop specifications to inform the design of innovative, functional, appealing products that respond to needs in a variety of situations

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: use a variety of approaches [for example, biomimicry and user-centred design] to generate creative ideas and avoid stereotypical responses

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: develop and communicate design ideas using annotated sketches, detailed plans, 3-D and mathematical modelling, oral and digital presentations

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: select from and use specialist tools, techniques, processes, equipment and machinery precisely, including computer-aided manufacture

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: select from and use a wider, more complex range of materials, components and ingredients, taking into account their properties

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: analyse the work of past and present professionals and others to develop and broaden their understanding

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: investigate new and emerging technologies

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: test, evaluate and refine their ideas and products against a specification, taking into account the views of intended users and other interested groups

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand developments in design and technology, its impact on individuals, society and the environment, and the responsibilities of designers, engineers and technologists

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand and use the properties of materials and the performance of structural elements to achieve functioning solutions

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand how more advanced mechanical systems used in their products enable changes in movement and force

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand how more advanced electrical and electronic systems can be powered and used in their products [for example, circuits with heat, light, sound and movement as inputs and outputs]

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: apply computing and use electronics to embed intelligence in products that respond to inputs [for example, sensors] and control outputs [for example, actuators] using programmable components [for example, microcontrollers]

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: use the basic principles of a healthy and varied diet to prepare dishes

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand where food comes from

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand and apply the principles of a healthy and varied diet

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: prepare and cook a variety of predominantly savoury dishes using a range of cooking techniques

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand seasonality, and know where and how a variety of ingredients are grown, reared, caught and processed

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand and apply the principles of nutrition and health

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: cook a repertoire of predominantly savoury dishes so that they are able to feed themselves and others a healthy and varied diet

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: become competent in a range of cooking techniques [for example, selecting and preparing ingredients; using utensils and electrical equipment; applying heat in different ways; using awareness of taste, texture and smell to decide how to season dishes and combine ingredients; adapting and using their own recipes]

statements.subject: design and technology
statements.text: understand the source, seasonality and characteristics of a broad range of ingredients
